rationale: Block 3 covers the clinical syndrome of nasal polyps; this question tests understanding of the characteristic laterality feature that distinguishes polyps from malignancy.

Block 7 covers diagnosis and differential diagnosis of nasal polyps; this statement tests the laterality rule — a high-yield known trap in ENT that distinguishes benign polyps from sinister pathology.
Block 8 covers orbital and intracranial complications of sinusitis; this question tests the ability to identify the most dangerous orbital complication requiring emergency surgical drainage.
Block 11 covers management of sinusitis; this statement tests a clinically important rule about antibiotic prescribing for acute rhinosinusitis — relevant to rational antibiotic use.
Block 6 explicitly covers the biopsy contraindication in JNA investigations — the single most critical known-trap rule in ENT. A TrueFalse anchored at this block directly encodes this rule.
Block 10 covers management of JNA; this question tests understanding of the role of pre-operative embolisation as the essential preparatory step before surgical resection.
Block 4 covers pathology and aetiology of sinonasal and nasopharyngeal tumours; this question tests understanding of the specific occupational and viral risk factors, which are high-yield for exams.
Block 7 covers diagnosis and staging; this statement tests the Ohngren line concept — a classic and high-yield staging landmark for maxillary sinus tumours.

Block 4 covers pathology and specific features of granulomatous nasal diseases; this question tests the ability to match histological findings to the correct granulomatous condition — a key diagnostic skill.

Block 10 covers management of granulomatous nasal diseases; this statement tests the treatment principle for leprosy — the most prevalent granulomatous disease affecting the nose in the Indian subcontinent.
